title: Underlying simplicial-set homotopy equivalence induces an abelian-group quasi-isomorphism
statement: Let $X,Y:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Ab}$ be simplicial abelian groups and $f:X\to Y$ a morphism [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. Write $UX,UY$ for their underlying simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. Suppose there is a simplicial-set map $g:UY\to UX$ such that $gf$ is homotopic to $\mathrm{id}_{UX}$ and $fg$ is homotopic to $\mathrm{id}_{UY}$. Here a homotopy from $a:K\to T$ to $b:K\to T$ is a simplicial map $h:K\times\Delta[1]\to T$ with $h(-,c_0)=a$ and $h(-,c_1)=b$, where $\Delta[1]_n=\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta([n],[1])$ and $c_0,c_1$ are the constant maps with values $0,1$; two maps are homotopic if they are joined by a finite chain of maps in which any two consecutive ones are related by a homotopy in one direction or the other. Neither $g$ nor the homotopies are assumed additive. Put $s(X)^{-n}=X_n$ for $n\geq0$, with differential $\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^id_i$ for $n>0$, and put $s(X)^r=0$ for $r>0$; define $s(Y)$ similarly. Then $s(f):s(X)\to s(Y)$ is a quasi-isomorphism: it induces an isomorphism on every cohomology group $H^r=\ker(d^r)/\operatorname{im}(d^{r-1})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tag 08P2 (lemma-homotopy-equivalence), lines 5883-5961; chain complexes reindexed as nonpositive cochains.

proof.text: For a simplicial abelian group $Z$, let $C(Z)_n=Z_n$ with alternating-face differential, and let $FZ$ have $(FZ)_n=\mathbb Z[Z_n]$, with each simplicial operator sending $[z]$ to the basis vector indexed by the corresponding operator on $z$. The evaluation maps $\epsilon_Z:FZ\to Z$, $[z]\mapsto z$, commute with every simplicial operator; since $f$ is additive, $f\epsilon_X=\epsilon_Y Ff$. Use the cited normalization convention $N(Z)_0=Z_0$, $N(Z)_n=\bigcap_{i=1}^n\ker d_i$ for $n>0$, with differential $d_0$ in positive degrees. For each $Z=X,Y,FX,FY$, the cited natural chain homotopy equivalence $N(Z)\to C(Z)$ induces a natural homology isomorphism: if two chain maps differ by $dh+hd$, their values on a cycle differ by the boundary $dh(z)$, so homotopy inverse maps induce inverse homology maps. Thus all comparison squares for $f,Ff,\epsilon_X,\epsilon_Y$ commute on homology. In this convention an $n$-cycle for $n>0$ has all its faces zero, while every element in degree zero is a cycle. No homology isomorphism between $FZ$ and $Z$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 08P2 (lemma-homotopy-equivalence), opening paragraph; normalization comparison also Tag 019C (lemma-quasi-isomorphism). We use the opposite-face convention of the cited existing node, with differential d_0.

proof.text: Apply the cited free-chain homotopy invariance with coefficient ring $\mathbb Z$ to each elementary homotopy in the finite chains joining $gf$ to $\mathrm{id}_{UX}$ and $fg$ to $\mathrm{id}_{UY}$. Each homotopy, in either direction, gives equality of the two induced maps on free-chain homology. Transitivity gives $H_n(C(Fg))H_n(C(Ff))=\mathrm{id}$ and $H_n(C(Ff))H_n(C(Fg))=\mathrm{id}$ for all $n\geq0$. Here $Fg:FY\to FX$ is defined on generators by $[y]\mapsto[g(y)]$; it is additive regardless of whether $g$ is additive, and free abelianization preserves composition and identity on generators. Hence $H_n(C(Ff))$ is bijective. The natural comparison of Step 1 makes $H_n(N(Ff))$ bijective as well.

source.place: Tag 08P2 (lemma-homotopy-equivalence), first paragraph: homology invertibility after free abelianization; extended along the finite homotopy chains in the statement.

proof.text: Fix $n\geq0$. To show surjectivity of $H_n(N(f))$, represent a target class $\eta$ by a normalized cycle $y\in N(Y)_n$. Put $\widetilde y=[y]-[0_n]\in(FY)_n$. If $n>0$, every face is $d_i\widetilde y=[d_i y]-[0_{n-1}]=0$, so $\widetilde y$ is a normalized cycle; if $n=0$, no face condition is required. Moreover $\epsilon_Y(\widetilde y)=y$. By Step 2 choose $\alpha\in H_n(N(FX))$ mapping to the class of $\widetilde y$. The commutative evaluation square of Step 1 now gives $H_n(N(f))(H_n(N(\epsilon_X))(\alpha))=\eta$. This proves surjectivity without assuming evaluation is a homology isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 08P2 (lemma-homotopy-equivalence), second paragraph: lift a normalized cycle by [y]-[0_n].

proof.text: For injectivity, represent a kernel class $\xi\in H_n(N(X))$ by a normalized cycle $x$. Since its image is zero, there is $y\in N(Y)_{n+1}$ with $d_0y=f_n(x)$; all $d_i y$ for $1\leq i\leq n+1$ vanish. As in Step 3, $\widetilde x=[x]-[0_n]$ is a normalized cycle lifting $x$. Put $\widetilde y=[y]-[0_{n+1}]$. Its higher faces vanish because $d_i\widetilde y=[0_n]-[0_n]=0$ for $i\geq1$, so it lies in $N(FY)_{n+1}$, and its differential is $d_0\widetilde y=[f_n(x)]-[0_n]=(Ff)_n(\widetilde x)$, where $f_n(0_n)=0_n$ uses additivity of $f$. Thus $H_n(N(Ff))$ kills the class of $\widetilde x$. Its injectivity from Step 2 makes this class zero; applying $H_n(N(\epsilon_X))$ shows $\xi=0$. This calculation also works for $n=0$, with $N(Y)_1=\ker d_1$ and boundary $d_0$.

source.place: Tag 08P2 (lemma-homotopy-equivalence), third paragraph: lift both the kernel cycle and its target boundary; translated to the d_0 normalization.

proof.text: Steps 3 and 4 prove that $H_n(N(f))$ is bijective for every $n\geq0$. By the natural isomorphisms of Step 1 this holds for $H_n(C(f))$. The complexes in the statement satisfy $s(Z)^{-n}=C(Z)_n$, with the same differential, so $H^{-n}(s(f))=H_n(C(f))$. For $r>0$ both cohomology groups are zero because $s(X)^r=s(Y)^r=0$. Therefore $s(f)$ induces an isomorphism on every cohomology group, which is exactly the stated quasi-isomorphism.

split_report.summary: Repaired the retained split after its initial dry run passed: removed the invalid identification of free-abelian homology with the original abelian-group homology. Followed the actual Stacks 08P2 argument: normalize all four simplicial abelian groups; obtain homology invertibility only for the free map; prove surjectivity and injectivity for the original map by explicit lifts [z]-[0], including the lift of a target boundary. The existing normalization uses kernels of d_1,...,d_n and differential d_0, and every boundary calculation is written in that convention. No new nodes are needed.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q58-883e2c153 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Stacks 08P2 (simplicial.tex 5884-5961) in full, plus the two cited Mathlib-leaf statements, which are the normalization N into C with the d_0 / ker d_{i≥1} convention, and free-chain homotopy invariance with R=ℤ. The item statement matches 08P2, with the zig-zag homotopy notion written out, no additivity assumed for g, and nothing weakened. Step 1: the evaluation square commutes because f is additive, and the step proves that a homotopy equivalence gives a homology isomorphism. Step 2: each link of the zig-zag gives an equality on homology, and functoriality of F then makes H(N(Ff)) bijective. Step 3: surjectivity via the lift [y]-[0_n], with every face zero in the d_0 convention and degree 0 checked. Step 4: injectivity via the lift [y]-[0_{n+1}], using f(0)=0 and d_0ỹ=Ff(x̃). These follow Stacks paragraphs 2 and 3, correctly adapted from Stacks' opposite-face convention. Step 5: the reindexing H^{-n}=H_n is correct, and positive degrees are zero. Edge cases checked: constant zero (this case is why the old FZ≅Z transport was wrong, and the new proof avoids it), constant A, and non-additive g. Duplicate search: the only 08P2 hits are the item and its citer cotangent-resolution-coherence. The surjective-boundary-lifting node is the converse, and the model-structure node lem-cbc-simplicial-module-model is not a restatement. No new nodes, no SGA, no cycle (both proof deps are leaves), proof_deps equals the union of uses, and every step is under 2000 characters. I accept the two generic tool_uses (normalization and free homotopy invariance). The citations.json named in the report is not in the commit, which is harmless. No changes made.

lean.statement: theorem quasiIso_alternatingFaceMap_of_underlying_homotopy_equivalence {X Y : SimplicialObject AddCommGrpCat.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (h : ∃ g : Y ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat.{u} ⟶ X ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat.{u}, Relation.EqvGen (fun a b ↦ Nonempty (SSet.Homotopy a b)) (Functor.whiskerRight f (forget AddCommGrpCat.{u}) ≫ g) (𝟙 (X ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat.{u})) ∧ Relation.EqvGen (fun a b ↦ Nonempty (SSet.Homotopy a b)) (g ≫ Functor.whiskerRight f (forget AddCommGrpCat.{u})) (𝟙 (Y ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat.{u}))) : QuasiIso (HomologicalComplex.extendMap ((alternatingFaceMapComplex AddCommGrpCat.{u}).map f) ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat)
